argument:
Bank Islam's 8.20x trailing earnings and vendor-reported 7.01% yield offer an income-and-value purchase case supported by stable H1 earnings. The issuer's corporate account reports 17.8% total capital and 0.98% gross impaired financing, together with 7.5% financing and 5.1% funding growth. These bank-appropriate observations provide more substance than a low multiple alone, while Q2 profit improved 9.8%.

The detailed attachment remains blocked, leaving CET1, liquidity and financing margin unverified; the corporate account is less detailed than full statements. Near-flat H1 earnings show that financing growth has not yet produced rapid profit growth. The disclosed asset-quality and capital metrics make resilience plausible, but the reported yield is not a payout guarantee. Weak price trend and low volume favor patient income ownership only if funding repricing and credit remain controlled, rather than an assumed near-term rerating.
key_points: Modest multiple and reported yield support conditional income value.
Issuer capital and impaired-financing metrics substantiate banking resilience.
Detailed capital/liquidity/margin gaps and modest H1 growth limit conviction.
